groups.title: Re-score: VOS as the whole runtime

items.title: Which VOS commit does EXP-1 score?
items.lead: The VOS report read one commit of the vos-core branch, and every gap row cites paths there. EXP-1 scores that commit unless this item says otherwise.
bullets: vos-core and master are different products, per the report's section 1
Scoring a later tip means re-reading every gap row first
Reversible: a later run can score another commit under its own run id
items.rec: the report's commit, because every gap row cites paths there.
options: vos-core at its tip when T-007-03 starts

items.title: Where does the purpose-built store sit?
items.lead: The purpose-built store is a module of CMP-STM's crate, rutent-stm, beside the reference host, behind that crate's Cargo feature purpose-built-store, off by default. EXP-1 keeps it there unless this item says otherwise.
bullets: The boundary check lets rutent-stm depend on the contracts; a new crate of ours may depend on nothing of ours
A crate of its own would mean an eighth package against DEC-2's seven, and widening the boundary check
With the flag off, CI's workspace build, lints, docs and tests don't compile it; a run turns it on
Reversible: moving it later changes its path, not its code
items.rec: inside rutent-stm behind the feature, because the boundary check allows it there without a change.
options: A module of rutent-stm behind the purpose-built-store feature (recommended)
A crate of its own, with DEC-2 and the boundary check widened to allow it

items.title: Which VOS commit does the re-score run?
items.lead: The re-score runs VOS as the whole runtime, the state machine a VOS program, at vos-core's tip when it was ruled: 5c7897582688ea93f8d02506bee8ea25da6b1458 (2026-11-06). GitHub's master is older than the first run's pin, so the commit is fetched by its SHA from vos-core.
bullets: The first run's pin, 1aadf44, stays scored as history under EXP-1-vos-20261107-1
The tip is 102 commits past the pin; its store layout was reset, so R-07a and R-07b cross the two
Reversible: a later run can score another commit under its own run id
items.rec: the tip, 5c78975, because the re-score asks how VOS does run the way it is meant to be run.
options: vos-core at the first run's pin, 1aadf44

items.title: Where do the scored re-score runs happen?
items.lead: On GitHub Actions' standard ubuntu-latest runner, through .github/workflows/exp1-vos.yml, with the nodes run on the runner host (never in a container, whose seccomp profile blocks userfaultfd). The harness fails closed: uname -r is 6.7 or later, a userfaultfd(UFFD_USER_MODE_ONLY) probe with write-protect succeeds, every node runs with VOS_PVM_BACKEND=recompiler and VOS_PVM_PERF_MAP=1, and each node's /tmp/perf-<pid>.map names the rutent program. The interpreter leg of R-09 runs with VOS_PVM_BACKEND=interpreter and asserts the map absent or empty. On three nodes each node's executors are floor(vCPUs / 3), at least 1. Binaries are built on the runner that runs them, with no cache.
bullets: The absence of VOS's fallback warning is not evidence: it is sent once per process, only on the default path
Local runs on macOS use the interpreter and are never scored
The note of every run records the kernel, the CPU, the vCPUs, the memory, the backend and the node build
items.rec: ubuntu-latest, asserted and fail closed, because the JIT needs Linux x86_64 on kernel 6.7 or later.
items.origin: EXP-1, T-007-03, 2026-11-07, before any re-score run

items.title: What does each new row pass on?
items.lead: The new rows' pass criteria, fixed before any run (the re-score brief, section 5). A cell is pass, fail, fail (by construction), a measured value with its unit, or n/a with its reason. fail (by construction) is a value of its own: outcome.md counts replication as one property, not as independent fails. G-39 gets no pass row: its recovery story is R-02, R-03 and R-08 together. Acknowledged means the Host client got an Ok reply.
bullets: R-01, the leader killed mid-submit on three nodes (each node its own process, kill -9; one placement deterministic through hold_commits or delay_commits, twenty at random points): passes when no acknowledged record is lost, the in-flight input is fully recorded or absent, resubmitting it returns the dedup result and not a second record, and the refusal log is consistent on all three nodes. pb: fail (by construction), one node; its restart on the same disk is timed for the note
R-02, one replica replaced from the survivors under a new key: passes when the new replica catches up and every journal is equal across the nodes. pb: fail (by construction), no replicas

R-03, one replica's data directory lost, then replaced under a new key, never from a copied store; once with the leader losing its data, once a follower: passes when no acknowledged record is lost. pb: restored from a copy taken at time T; the note counts the acknowledged records lost after T and whether their effects were released; fail if any were lost

R-04a, the last batch damaged on one node (truncated, or bytes flipped): passes when the store refuses to open, or the node rejoins and catches up; it never opens silently short. pb: the same damage, the same criterion

R-04b, the last batch damaged on the leader and one follower together, each node's last acknowledged sequence number recorded first: passes when the store refuses to open, or no acknowledged record is lost. pb: n/a, one node, so this is R-04a
R-04 with a durable-index watermark runs only if the VOS maintainer's watermark patch exists at the pinned commit; otherwise its cell reads n/a with the reason. The experiment does not patch VOS

R-05, concurrent submitters 1, 8 and 64, pb and VOS in the same job on the same runner: measured values, records per second, p50 and p99 latency, and fsyncs per record (counted in a separate run with strace -f -c -e trace=fsync,fdatasync,sync_file_range); the suite's guarantees hold under load. The numbers compare the two candidates on a noisy disk, not either against production

R-06a, the program upgraded over a running instance, one input in flight during the install: passes when state and journals survive, the in-flight input is recorded once or not at all, and the next input applies to the state from before the upgrade. pb: a redeploy of the binary

R-06b, a version installed whose state format changed: passes when rutent's program refuses it, through a format version kept in state, and never misreads bytes. pb: the same check on its layout version
R-07a, from the store deployment (the 1aadf44 adapter build) into the tip program through the swap stream: as H-13. pb: n/a
R-07b, record only, 1aadf44's data directory opened with the tip node (G-40): passes when it refuses cleanly, or opens with a journal byte-equal to the source; fails if it opens and misreads. pb: n/a

R-07c, the same program across two VOS commits through the swap stream: not runnable at the tip, no second vos-core commit builds this program yet; the cell reads n/a with that reason, never covered. pb: n/a

R-08, a timed halted export, then an import, at 1k, 10k and 100k records, paged at the stated page size: measured values, halt to export done, plus import start to ready on the new host; their sum is the RTO, the export interval the RPO, G-39's recovery figures. pb: the same procedure
R-09, gas and microseconds per step, JIT against interpreter: measured values, set against the 10M gas default. pb: microseconds per step only

H-01 to H-17 run against host contract 2.0.0 on one node and on three. H-02, H-06 and H-11 stop after computed: the program has computed and the commit is held (hold_commits, the faults build). H-17's native side is the original contracts/ and Probe, not the patched copies
items.rec: these criteria, as the brief fixed them, because a criterion set after a run can be fitted to it.
items.origin: EXP-1, T-007-03, 2026-11-07, before any re-score run

items.title: How is the state machine built for the VOS guest?
items.lead: vos-adapter/program/contracts-nostd/ and probe-nostd/ are generated by vos-adapter/nostd.sh: it copies contracts/src (and conformance's probe.rs) and applies a committed patch whose hunks touch only #![no_std], extern crate alloc, use lines and cfg attributes. Anything else goes in a named file of its own, listed in vos-adapter/program/SEPARATE and in every run note. contracts/ itself is never touched.
bullets: CI checks that the copy equals contracts/ plus the patch, that every hunk is plumbing only, and that the separate files are exactly the listed ones
The serialiser is not replaced: the guest uses serde_json built alloc-only. The byte-equality corpus runs anyway, through the guest, because the guest's serde_json is another build
H-17's native side folds with the original contracts/ and Probe
items.rec: a generated, plumbing-only copy, because contracts/ waits for the owner's click (DEC-20).
options: A generated copy with a plumbing-only patch (recommended)
A DEC-4 bump of contracts/ to no_std
items.origin: EXP-1, T-007-03, 2026-11-07, before any re-score run

items.title: What happens to the first run's adapter?
items.lead: The first run's adapter and journal, at VOS 1aadf44, stay in vos-adapter/adapter and vos-adapter/journal, buildable, because R-07a exports from that build and R-07b opens its data directory with the tip node. The tip build is new code beside it: vos-adapter/program (the VOS program) and vos-adapter/rt (the Host client and the runs).
bullets: The first run's note and cells stay as history
The two VOS revisions never share a crate graph: R-07a crosses them as a JSON-lines snapshot stream in a file
items.rec: keep it beside the new code, because R-07 needs it.
